texts.value: Catalyzes the transfer of the pyrophosphoryl group from ATP to the 1-hydroxyl of ribose-5-phosphate to form 5-phospho-ribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP), a key intermediate in the biosynthesis of several metabolites including nucleotides, dinucleotides and some amino acids (PubMed:37248548, PubMed:40295500, PubMed:8387514). Involved in the production of newly synthesized ATP/GTP through the purine biosynthesis pathway (PubMed:40295500)

Activated by magnesium (PubMed:8387514). Activated by inorganic phosphate (Pi) that binds D-ribose 5-phosphate binding site (PubMed:37248548, PubMed:8387514). Inhibited by GDP (PubMed:8387514). Feedback inhibition by purine nucleotides is less sensitive than inhibition by 2,3-diphosphoglycerate (PubMed:8387514). ADP can regulate enzyme activity through competitive inhibition and allosteric inhibition by affecting the conformation of regulatory flexible (RF) loop (PubMed:37248548). The ADP of allosteric site can interact with RF loop, leading to the regulation of ATP conformation in active site (PubMed:37248548). Competitive inhibition of ADP by binding to the ATP active site in the hexamer where also binds magnesium (PubMed:37248548). Thermal inactivation at 55 degrees Celsius (PubMed:8387514)
Optimum pH is 7.5 (PubMed:8387514). Optimum activity at pH 7.5 is obtained at a phosphate inorganic ion (Pi) concentration of 40- 50 mM (PubMed:8387514).
Metabolic intermediate biosynthesis; 5-phospho-alpha-D-ribose 1-diphosphate biosynthesis; 5-phospho-alpha-D-ribose 1-diphosphate from D-ribose 5-phosphate (route I): step 1/1

Homohexamer (PubMed:37248548, PubMed:40295500, Ref.9). Dimer of trimers (PubMed:40295500). In vitro, polymerizes into filaments of stacked hexamer, with D3 symmetry, through three interaction sites between two adjacent hexamers (PubMed:37248548). Filamentation is very important for its ribose phosphate diphosphokinase activity (PubMed:37248548)

RF loop can swing back and forth between active and allosteric sites to control ligands binding and regulates the ribose phosphate diphosphokinase activity (PubMed:37248548). The RF loop can help ATP enter the active site and participates in the allosteric regulation of ADP (PubMed:37248548)
Belongs to the ribose-phosphate pyrophosphokinase family
